Each of the 27 tools of the 4 S1000D Stack MCP servers has its own page. The pages are generated from what the servers return for `tools/list`, so they change when a server is updated. The configuration of each server and how to read its responses are on the [MCP servers](/s1000d-stack/mcp/) pages.

## s1000d-brex-mcp

The 5 tools of [s1000d-brex-mcp](/s1000d-stack/mcp/brex-mcp/) 0.9.0.

| Tool | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`explain_brex`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/brex/explain-brex/) | Lists the rules of a BREX. Returns the target (XPath), whether it may be used, the allowed values and their meaning, the severity level and the schemas the rule applies to. Narrow the list with `kind` (structure / notation / nonContext), `context` (schema name) and `search` (a string), and read it in parts with `offset` and `limit`. The header carries the whole `commonInfo` text whatever `limit` is; when reading further pages, pass `includeCommonInfo: false` to get only its length (`commonInfoLength`) |
| [`lookup_sns`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/brex/lookup-sns/) | Returns what a standard numbering system (SNS) code refers to, from a DMC or a code. When only a prefix matches, `exact: false` |
| [`lookup_value`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/brex/lookup-value/) | Returns what an element or attribute value means in the project and which values are allowed. Pass `value` to also get whether that value is allowed |
| [`list_notations`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/brex/list-notations/) | Returns the illustration and multimedia formats that may be used, split into the base set (`baseSet`), exclusions from the base set (`baseExcluded`) and the per-schema redefinitions and exclusions (`perContext`). Pass a schema name in `context` to get how that schema is restricted in `effectiveFor.mode`: `closed` means only the formats in `allowed` may be used, `open` means only the formats in `excluded` are forbidden (a BREX with exclusions only), and `unrestricted` means this BREX does not restrict formats |
| [`check_against_brex`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/brex/check-against-brex/) | Checks a data module against a BREX and returns each violation with its location (XPath and line number), actual value, rule ID, description and severity level. By default it follows the `brexDmRef` chain and checks against each layer separately |

## s1000d-verify-mcp

The 7 tools of [s1000d-verify-mcp](/s1000d-stack/mcp/verify-mcp/) 0.11.0.

| Tool | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`verify_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/verify/verify-data-module/) | Verifies one data module in the order well-formedness → XSD → BREX chain → references, and returns `verification` together with the details of each step (line numbers of XSD violations, locations of BREX violations, unresolved references and their reasons). Steps can be skipped with `skip` |
| [`validate_schema`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/verify/validate-schema/) | Runs XSD validation only. The XSD to use is chosen by the file name in `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation` and looked up in `xml_schema_flat/` under `S1000D_SPEC_DIR`. The issue is read from `Issue number:` at the top of `brex.xsd` |
| [`check_references`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/verify/check-references/) | Collects references of 5 kinds and returns whether each target exists, with a reason (`not-found` / `no-entity-declaration` / `file-not-found` / `no-such-id` / `no-csdb`). A `dmRef` to a chapter of the specification (model identification code `S1000D`) is not a broken reference, so it is reported separately |
| [`verify_csdb`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/verify/verify-csdb/) | Verifies the CSDB objects in a folder (DMC and PMC by default) in one run, and returns the verification status of each object and a count summary. Read the results in parts with `offset` and `limit`, and write the details to JSON with `reportPath` |
| [`suggest_fixes`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/verify/suggest-fixes/) | Runs the same verification as `verify_data_module` and returns candidate corrections for each finding. The server decides the candidates and adds where they come from and how certain they are (`exact` / `several` / `none`). If `product` is given, applicability that cannot be decided because the product lacks a value also gets candidate values. It does not apply any correction to the document |
| [`reconcile_dml`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/verify/reconcile-dml/) | Reconciles a data management list (DML) or a data dispatch note (DDN) with the CSDB and returns, per entry, `found` / `issue-mismatch` (the object exists but not the listed issue) / `not-found` / `not-checked`, plus the DMs and PMs that are in the CSDB but not listed in the DML (`notListed`; each row carries the issue of the file as `issueInfo`). Omit both `path` and `xml` to reconcile every DML and DDN in the CSDB. Values such as `dmlType` are not interpreted |
| [`list_schemas`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/verify/list-schemas/) | Returns the list of `xml_schema_flat/` folders found under `S1000D_SPEC_DIR` (issue, number of XSDs, schema names). Use it to find the cause of `schema-not-found` |

## s1000d-reader-mcp

The 6 tools of [s1000d-reader-mcp](/s1000d-stack/mcp/reader-mcp/) 0.16.0.

| Tool | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`list_data_modules`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/list-data-modules/) | Lists the data modules in the CSDB (and, if requested, PM, DML, DDN, IMF and UPF as well) with DMC, title, issue, language, schema name and the display text of their applicability. The list can be narrowed by model identification code, system code, information code, schema name and characters in the title. A DML or DDN row also carries its code, its entry or item count and a reconciliation summary against the CSDB (`found` / `issue-mismatch` / `not-found` / `not-checked`, and for a DML row `notListedCount`: the number of objects in the CSDB that the DML does not list). The per-entry result comes from `reconcile_dml` in `s1000d-verify-mcp` |
| [`read_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/read-data-module/) | Reads one data module as structure: the identification and status section, the content tree, references (with titles) and the verification status. When `product` is passed, each block is marked `applicable` / `notApplicable` / `undetermined`. With `includeLocation: true`, every node carries `location` (`path`, `line`, `column`) |
| [`read_publication_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/read-publication-module/) | Reads a publication module as a table of contents: the `pmEntry` tree and the resolved target (file, title, issue) of each `dmRef` / `pmRef` |
| [`resolve_reference`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/resolve-reference/) | Resolves a DMC, PMC or ICN to a file in the CSDB. For an ICN it also returns the DOCTYPE declaration of the referencing file (file name and NOTATION) |
| [`describe_applicability`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/describe-applicability/) | Returns the applicability vocabulary: the product attributes of the ACT, the conditions of the CCT, the products of the PCT, the `applic` statements in the document (id and display text), and the attributes to which the PCT assigns no value. Nothing is evaluated here |
| [`read_icn_metadata`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/read-icn-metadata/) | Reads an ICN metadata file (IMF): ICN, issue, title, keywords, security classification, and a list of the items in the status section |

## s1000d-writer-mcp

The 9 tools of [s1000d-writer-mcp](/s1000d-stack/mcp/writer-mcp/) 0.9.0.

| Tool | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`build_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/build-data-module/) | Builds one data module from one draft (descriptive, procedural, process, fault isolation or publication module) and the numbering rules. After building, it verifies the XSD, BREX and references, and automatically applies only the `exact` fixes, up to `maxFixRounds` times (default 3). The fixes that remain are returned in `fixes[]` with candidates |
| [`convert_manual`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/convert-manual/) | Converts an experiential manual ([`@shuji-bonji/experiential-manual-model`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@shuji-bonji/experiential-manual-model)) into one data module per Topic and one publication module. Each data module is built and verified in the same flow as `build_data_module`. References between data modules, publication modules and ICNs are resolved against the CSDB with the data modules built in this call laid over it. What the conversion cannot express is returned as counts in `notRepresented` |
| [`apply_fixes`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/apply-fixes/) | Applies to an existing data module the fixes selected from the candidates returned in `fixes[]`. A selection must be a copy of a candidate; a value outside the candidates, or a value that does not fit a range, is put into `rejected[]` with a reason. The result is verified again |
| [`edit_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/edit-data-module/) | Changes the structure of an existing procedural or descriptive data module: inserts, removes or moves a node. Places are `location.path` values, and a node to insert is a draft node (`step`, `para`, `admonition`, `listItem`). Only the edited ranges of the original text are rewritten; every other character stays as it was. Without `marking`, it changes neither the issue information nor change markup (`changeType` and so on). With `marking`, it adds change markup to an in-work issue. A result with XSD errors that the edits introduced is not written |
| [`start_revision`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/start-revision/) | Starts an in-work issue of a released data module. `inWork` becomes `01`, `issueNumber` stays, and `issueType` is the value you give (`changed`, `revised` or `status`; the server does not choose it). The change markup and the reasons for update of the previous issue are removed, and elements marked `changeType="delete"` are taken out. The released issue is not changed: the in-work issue is written as a new file. If you pass `reason`, one reason for update is added in the same call |
| [`add_reason_for_update`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/add-reason-for-update/) | Adds one reason for update (`reasonForUpdate`) to the identification and status section of an in-work issue. It does not touch the content and adds no change markup. Use it to write the reason of a change that has no change markup (an editorial change `urt01`, or an issue whose `issueType` is `revised` or `status`) |
| [`create_comment`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/create-comment/) | Builds and verifies a comment data module (`comment`). If the sequence number is omitted, it is the next number in the CSDB |
| [`extract_segments`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/extract-segments/) | Takes out of a data module the sentences that a person reads (titles, paragraphs, steps, warnings, table cells, figure titles) for translation. Inline elements are replaced by the placeholders `{1}` `{2}`, and `skeletonHash`, used to check the skeleton, is returned |
| [`apply_segments`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/apply-segments/) | Puts translated sentences back into the original data module. The DMC stays the same and only the language changes. If the data module has changed since the sentences were taken out, it stops with `skeleton-mismatch` |
